items.rationale: Sections 5.2.6–5.2.7 cover necessary dismantling and refitting for access or drying. Case 46 supports €90 for one service.
Section 5.2.7 covers the documented period of necessary drying. The seven days billed are consistent with the reported drying period and benchmark at €313 gross.
Section 7.4.4 requires an itemised materials list, and the surcharge is expressly unexplained. The conditional benchmark is €39 if qualifying materials are documented.
Sections 5.2.6 and 7.14(c) allow necessary reinstatement with mineral-wool insulation in the original diameter. One piece benchmarks at €26.
Section 5.2.2 covers necessary debris disposal once and allows the first charge when trades duplicate it. The first listed disposal charge benchmarks at €60.
Section 5.2.6 covers levelling the affected substrate as part of making good. The benchmark for one material line is €38.
Section 5.2.6 covers necessary substrate preparation, but §7.4.1 bars labour already billed separately. If this line represents distinct preparation, 2.78 m² at about €30/m² gives €83.
Section 5.2.6 expressly covers necessary service openings to reach the affected element. The comparable opening in Case 46 supports €19.

The tiles are at the format limit in §7.14(d), with like-for-like grade required by §7.1.6. Five tiles provide 4.05 m² before cutting; at about €52/m², the gross threshold is €211 if all five were needed.

The tiles exceed the 90 × 90 cm limit in §7.14(d), and §3.5(f) bars partial payment for an item exceeding that threshold. If assessed instead on a standard-grade equivalent basis, the benchmark is about €211, with no second tile allowance for the same area.
Sections 5.2.6 and 7.14(a) allow standard sanitary silicone joints as part of making good. At about €13/m, 3.6 m gives €47 gross.
Section 7.4.2 allows the tiler's first travel charge on this document. The single charge benchmarks at €81.
Section 7.4.1 covers necessary labour at customary rates, excluding hours already included in unit or flat rates. The full 14-hour line benchmarks at €1,239 if the hours are distinct and documented.

items.description: Remove basement drywall and insulation wool
items.rationale: Section 5.2.6 covers necessary removal in the affected basement, subject to substantiation of the flat rate under §7.4.4. Comparable removal in Case 46 supports €90 gross, excluding duplicate waste handling.
Sections 5.2.6 and 7.1.5 cover removal of plaster affected by the basement escape of water. The single billed unit benchmarks at €29.
Section 3.5(b) excludes work outside the documented damage area, and the attic work is expressly unrelated. The €29 figure is only a conditional one-unit removal benchmark.
Sections 3.5(d) and 5.2.2 bar this second charge for the same disposal already billed on line 5. The €60 figure is the benchmark for a qualifying disposal charge, not an additional allowance.
